editorial_policy.rule_1: Every record separates documented_fact, reasoned_reconstruction and game_fiction. A briefing may not present game_fiction as a recorded event.
editorial_policy.rule_2: sources[] must name a real, checkable source. An empty sources[] with review_status 'pending_citation' is the ONLY permitted placeholder. Inventing a citation is a release blocker.
editorial_policy.rule_3: Player outcomes may change modelled local conditions. They never edit the text of a documented_fact record.
editorial_policy.rule_4: No record may attribute invented dialogue, testimony or audio to a real person. Fictional characters are flagged is_fictional: true.
editorial_policy.rule_5: Sensitive settings (ghettos, camps, extermination centres, hiding places) require sign-off by a named specialist reviewer before the chapter that uses them may enter production.

confidence_scale.high: Date and outline are uncontroversial across standard reference works. Still requires a citation before release.
confidence_scale.medium: Outline is well established; specific figures, local detail or exact timing need a specialist to fix.
confidence_scale.low: Working assumption used for scheduling only. Must be replaced or removed before the chapter ships.

records.gameplay_use: Opens the campaign. Sets Warsaw's control, supply and civil-restriction state for chapter one.
Changes Warsaw district access rules, checkpoint placement, ration availability and civilian group restrictions by date.
records.treatment_note: Represented through community institutions, households, work, smuggling and mutual aid. The player's agency is to help people move, communicate and survive, never to administer persecution.

records.gameplay_use: London chapters use civil-defence, shelter and relief objectives. Combat is not the primary verb.
Reference context ONLY. It is cited in the in-game historical panel. No playable district reconstructs this building, and no fictional attic in this game may be presented as it.
records.treatment_note: The brief asks for Anne Frank-inspired hiding-place themes. This project implements that as an original fictional household in an original building, with the real history credited separately and never merged into the fiction.

records.gameplay_use: Opens the North Africa theatre and changes control and supply routing around Tunis.
Closes Axis control of the Tunis region and switches the district to a liberated-city state with different ambience and restrictions.
Salonica chapters are set before and during this period. Objectives concern warning, documentation, concealment and escape routes.
records.treatment_note: The community is represented through its Ladino-speaking households, trades, synagogues and institutions. End dates and transport counts must be fixed by the specialist reviewer; the medium confidence flag exists because this project has not yet verified them.

records.gameplay_use: Authored chapter. Bunkers, cellars and rooftop routes. Outcomes affect who the player can still reach afterwards; they do not alter the recorded outcome of the uprising.
records.treatment_note: Agency is granted to the defenders. The chapter may not offer a 'victory' that contradicts the historical record; its authored outcomes are who survives in the fiction and what the network retains.

records.gameplay_use: Opens the Normandy theatre, the sabotage and reconnaissance mission family and the first production district.
Late Warsaw chapter. Distinct from the 1943 ghetto uprising record; the two must never be presented as one event.
Home-front chapter: fundraising, affidavit and paperwork chains, shipping relief parcels, locating relatives. No combat, no occupation.
records.treatment_note: Marked reasoned_reconstruction because the chapter composites typical organisational activity rather than one documented office. The specific named organisations must be fixed by the researcher before this chapter ships.

records.gameplay_use: An original fictional household in a concealed upper room. Carries the hiding-place mechanics: sound discipline, light exposure, ration division, interpersonal tension.
records.treatment_note: Explicitly labelled fiction in the journal. Inspired by documented hiding, not a reconstruction of any real place or family.
